transcript:
Meeting header:
2027-06-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Morris (AstraMed - Head of Infrastructure), Priya Shah (AstraMed - Security Lead), Tom Reyes (AstraMed - Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on private VPC deployment options for Redwood Private. Main focus: networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region residency (us-west-2 / eu-west-1), cross-account connectivity, and security controls (KMS, audit logs, SSO).

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll hand off to Ethan for the deep-dive but quick introductions first.
00:08 Lena (AstraMed): Hi, Lena here. We run a mix of EHR workloads and analytics, pretty latency-sensitive for some patient-facing features.
00:15 Priya (AstraMed): Priya, security. We'll own the compliance checklist.
00:18 Tom (AstraMed): Tom, platform, I'll be the hands-on eng.
00:22 Ethan (Redwood SE): Great. So objective for today is to understand your networking constraints and what you need from a Private deployment - peering, PrivateLink, region limits, etc.
00:37 Lena: High-level: we want Redwood in our VPCs (or connected) so data never traverses public internet. Primary region us-west-2, some EU data residency in eu-west-1 for EU patients. We also have strict SAML SSO + S3 restrictions.
00:55 Maya: What's your timeline like?
00:58 Lena: We're aiming to pilot in August, production by Q4 if security checks out.
01:05 Ethan: Good. A few approaches: 1) Cross-account VPC peering/transit gateway to Redwood-managed VPCs, 2) PrivateLink / Interface VPC Endpoints into Redwood's control plane, or 3) Full private deployment where Redwood's control plane is in your account (Private - on-prem style). We usually recommend PrivateLink or dedicated private deployment for regulated workloads.
01:45 Priya: Can you expand on PrivateLink vs peering pros/cons?
01:50 Ethan: Sure. VPC peering is simpler for L3 route-based comms but can get hairy cross-region and with many peers. PrivateLink gives interface endpoints — TLS over AWS backbone, simpler for per-service IP whitelisting, no route table overlap, better for multi-account. Transit gateway scales for many VPCs. Our deployed options depend on whether you want Redwood-managed infra or customer-managed nodes.
02:20 Tom: We have multiple AWS accounts (prod, staging, analytics). For secret management we use AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys. How does Redwood integrate KMS keys?
02:34 Ethan: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) for encrypting data at rest in Private deployments; for hosted we keep keys but can do envelope encryption. For Private (VPC/on-prem) we can integrate with your KMS via IAM roles and grant decrypt only to the nodes in your account. There might be some differences if you want HSM-only operations.
02:58 Priya: Audit logs - we need all inference logs sent to our S3 with retention 7 years and immutable logs. Is that supported?
03:08 Maya: We can ship audit logs to your S3 via cross-account write or you can pull via API; for Private we can write directly into customer S3. We have retention and WORM-friendly options; need to validate with compliance but we do SOC2 and have audit hooks.
03:30 Lena: Ok good. Region stuff: some of our EU data must stay in eu-west-1; can Redwood run model endpoints in eu-west-1 while the control plane is in us-west-2?
03:44 Ethan: Yes — we can deploy inference nodes in multiple regions and route requests by policy. For Private deployments customers typically want per-region nodes. If you need data residency guarantees, we recommend fully isolated per-region node pools in your account or dedicated regional deployments.
04:05 Speaker 1: quick q: latency between user and the model vs cost — any guidance?
04:10 Ethan: Latency is driven by region proximity and batching. Per-call latency will improve if you colocate nodes in the same region as your frontend. There's a small cost overhead per region for reserved capacity but it reduces cross-region egress.
04:35 Tom: Network architecture — we have strict egress rules: only allow specific IPs outbound, no open internet. How do we lock down nodes?
04:44 Ethan: For Private nodes in your VPC you control egress; Redwood's runtime can operate in private subnets with NAT or via VPC endpoints to reach external systems if required. If you want zero egress, we can support air-gapped on-prem deployments, but that adds ops complexity.
05:08 Priya: For PrivateLink, what endpoints does Redwood require? We prefer to manage interface endpoints per-service.
05:14 Ethan: We'll provide a list — control plane API, metrics ingestion, model registry endpoints. Each will map to an interface endpoint service name. PrivateLink avoids broad route table changes and works cross-account.
05:30 Lena: We're worried about cross-account roles and principle of least privilege — can you share the exact IAM role policy you require?
05:38 Maya: Yes, we'll share a baseline IAM trust policy and least-priv policies. Ethan: note that for peering/transit gateway we need route entries only; for PrivateLink we need acceptance of the endpoint and security group rules.
06:02 Tom: Any special subnet sizing? Our subnets are /24; will that be sufficient?
06:08 Ethan: Depends on concurrent node count; a /24 per AZ is usually fine for initial pilot. We'll provide guidance. Also note IP allocation for interface endpoints consumes IPs from your subnet.
06:25 Priya: What about SSO and RBAC? We use Okta with SCIM.
06:30 Ethan: Redwood supports SAML SSO + SCIM user provisioning for RBAC mapping. For Private we can federate to your IdP; we recommend a group-based mapping to roles (admin, dev, ops).
06:45 Lena: What about model artifacts — where are models stored and who can access them?
06:50 Ethan: In Private deployments we store model artifacts in customer-managed object storage or in encrypted Redwood buckets with access controls; for strict data residency you can host model artifacts in your S3 and we mount or reference them.
07:10 Tom: Are there examples of customers doing multi-region with PrivateLink?
07:15 Ethan: Yes — a couple of health and fintech customers. We typically set up regional endpoint services plus a central control plane (or control plane in customer account) and route by region. There can be a small additional latency (10-30ms) if control plane calls cross regions but inference stays local.
07:40 Speaker 1: transcription glitch - sometimes I see 'KV cache' as 'KV cash' in notes.
07:45 Ethan: yeah our transcript sometimes swaps words, noted.
07:50 Priya: Encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between nodes and control plane?
07:55 Ethan: We use TLS 1.2/1.3. Mutual TLS can be enabled in Private deployments if needed, otherwise we rely on AWS networking + IAM.
08:12 Lena: For pilot scope — what are the minimum steps to get a POC?
08:18 Maya: Typical POC: 2-3 endpoints in us-west-2, PrivateLink or peering set up, 1 benchmarking script from your side, sample data for evals (anonymized), 4-week pilot. We'll share a template SOW.
08:36 Tom: Benchmarking — can Redwood run throughput tests inside our VPC?
08:40 Ethan: Yes, we can run a load generator in the same VPC or use your tester to avoid external traffic. We'll coordinate security.
08:50 Priya: Compliance questions: SOC2 Type II evidence? ISO?
08:55 Maya: We'll send SOC2 Type II report, ISO posture, pen test summary. For Private we also provide deployment hardening docs.
09:08 Lena: Network peering: we use Transit Gateway heavily. Is transit gateway supported?
09:14 Ethan: Yes — we can peer to your transit gateway; we've done TGW attachments for large fleets. That often simplifies routing for many VPCs.
09:28 Tom: Do you support AWS PrivateLink in eu-west-1 from your account, or do we need Redwood to publish the endpoint service in eu region?
09:36 Ethan: Redwood can publish endpoint services in specific regions. For Private deployments in your account we'll create endpoint services in that region; for Redwood-managed endpoint services we can support cross-account PrivateLink but it must be published in eu-west-1 for low latency.
09:55 Priya: Data egress costs between regions — how does that get billed?
10:02 Maya: For Dedicated/Private in customer account, inter-region egress is within your AWS billing; Redwood pricing for hosted handles cross-region differently. We'll include cost guidance in the follow-up.
10:18 Lena: Who owns the nodes in Dedicated vs Private? Clarify language: Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware reserved for you; Private can be Redwood-managed in customer VPC or fully customer-managed?
10:30 Ethan: Correct. Dedicated: Redwood manages node fleet in our accounts/regions but reserved to you. Private: two models — Redwood-managed nodes deployed into your VPC (we run control plane pieces in your network or peered manner), or customer-managed where nodes are in your account and you control images and scaling.
10:52 Tom: For customer-managed nodes, what's the upgrade path? Can Redwood push runtime patches?
10:58 Ethan: With customer-managed we provide an operator (Helm/Ansible) and upgrade manifests. We can automate upgrades with your approval window.
11:10 Priya: Any certifications for HSM integrations?
11:12 Ethan: We can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or external HSM via KMS; specific attestation depends on your provider. We'll need to validate in the SOW.
11:30 Lena: Ok, let's capture the immediate blockers: we need SOC2 docs, network diagram, and a deployment diagram showing PrivateLink vs peering.
11:40 Maya: We'll get those over. Ethan: I'll draft the preliminary network diagram and a checklist for your security team.
11:48 Tom: Also need a clear list of required security groups and ports for the interface endpoints.
11:53 Ethan: Yes, common ports are 443 for API, 9200-ish for metrics if we expose Prometheus scrape endpoints, but we'll provide exact list.
12:10 Priya: Are there any managed firewall appliances required? we use Palo Alto in-line.
12:15 Ethan: You can front nodes with your firewall; if you want the nodes to be private we recommend using NGFW in front of subnets. We can work with your network team.
12:32 Lena: Last thing: what are typical lead times to get PrivateLink services published in our account?
12:37 Ethan: If configurations and accounts are ready, usually 1-2 weeks to stand up endpoint services + test. If we need custom images or HSM provisioning it takes longer.
12:50 Maya: Great. recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2 + network diagrams, Ethan will prepare deployment diagram and checklist, Lena will share CIDRs and account IDs. We'll schedule SE deep dive and bench in 2 weeks.
13:10 Lena: Sounds good. Thanks all.
13:14 Priya: Thanks.
13:16 Meeting end (notes): brief crosstalk and transcript clean-up needed.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some words mistranscribed (proper nouns), occasional speaker attribution errors.
